table_title: For each Apollo lunar-landing mission (the six Apollo missions whose spacecraft successfully landed on the Moon), list each crew member with their role, the year of the mission, and the astronaut's birth year.
db_analog: SELECT m.mission_name AS mission, c.astronaut_name AS astronaut, c.role, m.year_of_mission, a.birth_year AS astronaut_birth_year FROM apollo_missions m JOIN apollo_mission_crew_assignments c ON c.mission_id = m.id JOIN apollo_astronauts a ON a.name = c.astronaut_name WHERE m.outcome = 'successful_lunar_landing' ORDER BY m.year_of_mission ASC, m.mission_name ASC, role_order ASC
temporal_note: Wikipedia 'List of Apollo astronauts' (master article) and 6 per-mission Wikipedia articles (Apollo 11, 12, 14, 15, 16, 17), all accessed 2026-05-11. The universe is the 6 Apollo missions that successfully landed on the Moon: Apollo 11 (July 1969 — first landing), Apollo 12 (Nov 1969), Apollo 14 (Feb 1971), Apollo 15 (July-Aug 1971), Apollo 16 (April 1972), Apollo 17 (Dec 1972 — final landing). Apollo 13 is excluded (abortive landing — oxygen tank explosion en route); Apollo 8 and 10 are excluded (orbital-only missions, no landing attempt). All mission years use the calendar year of the lunar surface activity. None of the 6 Apollo lunar-landing missions actually spanned a year boundary in their mission duration: Apollo 11 (July 1969), Apollo 12 (Nov 1969), Apollo 14 (Jan 31 - Feb 9, 1971 — entirely 1971), Apollo 15 (July 26 - Aug 7, 1971 — entirely 1971), Apollo 16 (April 1972), Apollo 17 (Dec 7-19, 1972 — entirely 1972). The Year column rule is therefore unambiguous: every mission's full duration falls within a single calendar year. Astronaut birth years are from the 'List of Apollo astronauts' article's biographical tabulation, which lists every Apollo astronaut with their birth date. All facts are stable historical record and will not drift over time.
_extraction_notes: Multi_hop instance: 3-entity-set chained join. Apollo missions → mission crew assignments → astronaut biographical attributes. Universe = 6 successful Apollo lunar-landing missions × 3 crew members each (Commander, Lunar Module Pilot, Command Module Pilot) = 18 rows. Of the 18 astronauts, 12 walked on the Moon (CMDR + LMP for each of 6 missions); 6 stayed in lunar orbit (CMP role). The Role column captures this distinction. Per-mission crew (cycle-0): Apollo 11 (Armstrong CMDR, Aldrin LMP, Collins CMP, 1969); Apollo 12 (Conrad, Bean, Gordon, 1969); Apollo 14 (Shepard, Mitchell, Roosa, 1971); Apollo 15 (Scott, Irwin, Worden, 1971); Apollo 16 (Young, Duke, Mattingly, 1972); Apollo 17 (Cernan, Schmitt, Evans, 1972). Birth years (cycle-0): Armstrong 1930, Aldrin 1930, Collins 1930, Conrad 1930, Bean 1932, Gordon 1929, Shepard 1923 (oldest), Mitchell 1930, Roosa 1933, Scott 1932, Irwin 1930, Worden 1932, Young 1930, Duke 1935, Mattingly 1936 (youngest), Cernan 1934, Schmitt 1935, Evans 1933. Schema: composite PK (Mission, Astronaut) with 18 unique pairs; 5 cols (2 keys + 1 categorical Role + 2 numeric Years). Sort order: (Year ASC, Mission ASC, Role-order ASC where Role-order is Cmdr=0/LMP=1/CMP=2). Multi-hop chain: source_urls[0] master List-of-Apollo-astronauts → source_urls[1-6] per-mission crew → astronaut name → birth year (via master article's biographical table). Cycles 1+2+3 + Fields-Medal-cycles lessons applied upfront: (a) composite PK explicit (Mission, Astronaut); (b) per-row Wikipedia citation via per-mission article (crew assignments + year) and master astronaut article (birth years); (c) explicit relation commitment in title and db_analog (mission landed = spacecraft successfully landed on Moon surface; Role = crew role per mission; Year of Mission = calendar year of lunar surface activity); (d) universe filter explicit (excludes Apollo 13 abort, excludes orbital-only Apollo 8/10). Multi-wiki source plan (7 URLs): 1 master + 6 per-mission articles.
